 ORDER With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, heard finally at Motion stage.

2 . This appeal has been filed by the appellant-Insurance Company under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 24.08.2023 passed in MACC.No.329/2020 by 8th M.A.C.T., Sagar, District- Sagar seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant after referring to deposition of applicant's witness Ramkeshav Bharadwaj and ITR Returns - Ex. P/18 , 19 and 20 and also relying upon Smt. Anjali and Others Vs.
Lokendra Rathod and Others, 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 1012; (2) Order dated 06.10.2023 passed by Hon'ble High Court of M.P. at Jabalpur in M.A.No.1669/2015 - Kasak and others Vs. Rajesh and others, (3) Order dated 21.08.2023 passed by Hon'ble High Court of M.P. at Jabalpur i n M.A.

sentences.text: In view of above, income of the appellant /deceased should have been determined on the basis of ITRs-Ex. - P/18 to P/20.

Tribunal has determined monthly income as Rs.10,000/-
treating him as skilled labourer.
Therefore it is urged that deceased's income be determined as per ITRs and accordingly compensation be suitably enhanced.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent /insurance company submits that appellant have not filed any documents pertaining to money lending business run by the deceased and no money lending license has been filed.
No officer from the income tax office has been examined to prove ITRs.

sentences.text: Therefore the tribunal has not committed any error in not determining deceased's income on the basis of ITRs.
Hence no interference is required in the findings recorded by the tribunal.
Therefore appeal filed by the appellant is dismissed.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and pursed the record of the case.

6. Sole issue involved in the case is whether in the facts and the circumstances of the case deceased's income should have been determined on the basis of I.T.R. - Ex.-P/18 to P/ 20 filed by the appellants.
7. With respect to above, primary issue before this Court is whether appellants have succeeded in proving documents- ITRs- Ex.-P/18 to P/ 20.
No officer from the Income Tax Office has been examined to prove that deceased has filed above ITRs in Income Tax Department.
No other document showing filing of above ITR Returns in Income Tax Department has been filed on behalf of appellants in the instant case.
Further, as per appellants' case, deceased was running a business of money lending and he was also having license thereof.

But appellants have not filed documents relating to money lending business including Money Lending Licence nor any account/Ledger etc.
have been filed to show that deceased was running business of money lending.
No explanation has been furnished for non-filing of above material documents.

8. Therefore, in the absence of above material documents /evidence, just on the basis of - Ex. P/18,
19 and 20 deceased's income cannot be determined on the basis of above ITR Returns.
9. Perusal of Smt. Anjali and others (Supra) reveals that therein income tax inspector was examined with respect to ITR.

So far as MA No.1669/2015 and MA No.4742/2011 are concerned, from above it does not transpire that as to what evidence was led in these cases for proving ITR Returns/source of income etc. of deceased.
Therefore, principles laid down in above pronouncements do not help the appellant in any way in instant case.

10. Hence in view of above, in this court's opinion, learned tribunal has not committed any illegality in determining deceased's income treating him as skilled person and determining his monthly income @ Rs.10,000/-.
No interference is required in the findings recorded by the tribunal with respect to above.
10. Hence appeal filled by the appellants is dismissed.
